question: Assume today is 2026-09-05. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of new passenger cars (Pkw) registered in Germany in September 2026, as it will be first reported in the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt's (KBA) monthly press release on vehicle registrations.

target.what: Number of new passenger cars (Pkw) with first registration in Germany during September 2026, as reported by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA) in its monthly press release on vehicle registrations (Fahrzeugzulassungen). Counts new Pkw first registrations (Neuzulassungen), domestic Germany, all brands, p
target.cadence: monthly press release, typically published in the first week of the following month
target.caveats: Target period is future relative to the 2026-09-05 cutoff; only forecasts/partial signals available. Working interpretation: KBA 'Neuzulassungen von Personenkraftwagen' monthly total for September 2026 (calendar month, domestic registrations). Alternative interpretations: including or excluding Pkw

candidates.hypothesis: September registrations follow a seasonal pattern; the target equals the September 2025 level adjusted for the 2026 trend and any known shocks. Historical September values and recent monthly values (Jan-Aug 2026) anchor the estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: KBA monthly Pkw Neuzulassungen for September in each year 2019-2025, plus monthly values Jan-Aug 2026 (or latest available before cutoff). Minimum: September 2024, September 2025, and 2026 YTD monthly totals.

candidates.hypothesis: Germany's share of EU/ACEA new passenger car registrations is relatively stable; Germany September = (EU September total) × (Germany share). ACEA publishes monthly EU registrations, sometimes before or alongside KBA.
candidates.data_to_find: ACEA monthly new passenger car registrations for EU and Germany, September 2025 and 2026 YTD; Germany share of EU total. Minimum: Germany share in recent months and any September 2026 EU preliminary figure.
search_hints: ACEA new passenger car registrations September 2026
ACEA Germany share EU car registrations 2026

candidates.hypothesis: VDA, ifo, and analyst forecasts for German 2026 car market imply a September level; a full-year 2026 forecast divided by seasonal shares gives September. Direction depends on forecast revisions.
candidates.data_to_find: VDA/ifo/analyst forecasts for German 2026 passenger car registrations (full year), and any monthly or September-specific forecasts published before 2026-09-05. Minimum: one credible full-year 2026 forecast plus historical September share of annual total.

candidates.hypothesis: New registrations in September are constrained by vehicles delivered from dealer stock and prior order books; order intake and production in preceding months predict September deliveries. High order backlog implies higher registrations.
candidates.data_to_find: German passenger car order intake (VDA/ifo), domestic production and exports for Jun-Aug 2026, dealer inventory levels. Minimum: order backlog trend and production trend for mid-2026.

candidates.perspective: Policy and incentive changes affecting September 2026
candidates.hypothesis: Changes to EV purchase incentives (Umweltbonus/company car taxation), CO2 fleet regulation timing, or fuel prices can pull registrations forward or push them back, altering the September level relative to seasonal baseline.
candidates.data_to_find: Any German EV subsidy or company-car tax changes effective around Q3/Q4 2026; CO2 regulation milestones; known pull-forward/pull-back effects. Minimum: confirmation of whether a policy change falls in September or October 2026.

candidates.hypothesis: September typically accounts for a stable share (~8-9%) of annual German Pkw registrations; annual 2026 total × September share = target. Useful when a full-year forecast exists.
candidates.data_to_find: Historical monthly shares of annual Pkw registrations for Germany, September share 2019-2025, and annual 2026 forecast. Minimum: September share averaged over recent years.

candidates.perspective: Media and search interest in car buying
candidates.hypothesis: Search and media attention to car purchases correlates with registration volume with a short lag; elevated attention in September 2026 signals above-baseline registrations. Used only as a directional adjustment.
candidates.data_to_find: Google Trends for 'Neuwagen'/'Auto kaufen' in Germany for Aug-Sep 2026 vs prior years; automotive media coverage volume. Minimum: relative trend direction.

assumptions.name: September 2026 YoY change factor vs September 2025

assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 tracks the 2026 YTD trend rather than a new shock (subsidy pull-forward, CO2 regulation timing).
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp September 2026 collapse or surge (e.g., August 2026 YoY far from +1 to +5%, or a policy change pulling registrations into/out of September).

assumptions.falsified_by: Historical monthly data showing September's share consistently outside 7.5-9.2%.

methods.label: m1

p141.role: September 2025 German Pkw new registrations (235,528), the base level

a1.role: change factor from September 2025 to September 2026

methods.rationale: YoY-scaling route: September 2025 base (p141) scaled by the 2026 momentum factor a1. Anchored on the strongest available evidence (2026 YTD +5%, August +3%, EV surge). Main failure mode: September 2025 was an unusually strong month, so a mean-reverting September 2026 could undershoot.
methods.error: input p141: id p141 unknown or discarded

methods.label: m2

p75.role: Germany Pkw new registrations January-April 2026 cumulative (948,567), annualised to a 2026 full-year level

methods.rationale: Base-rate route: annualise Jan-Apr 2026 volume (p75 x 12/4) and apply the September seasonal share a2. The 4-month divisor is expressed via k_months_per_year so no bare numeric constant appears. Independent of the September 2025 base but shares the 2026 momentum assumption; failure mode is that Jan-Apr annualisation ignores later-month seasonality and the strong EV-driven H2.

kept.name: September 2026 YoY change factor vs September 2025
kept.rationale: 2026 YTD registrations are +5% (p170) and August +3% (p169); EV-led strength (p176, p179) and the new 2026 subsidy (p89, p90) support a modest positive YoY, but September 2025 was already a strong +12.8% base (p142), so the factor is centred near +5% with wide uncertainty.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 tracks the 2026 YTD/August momentum rather than reverting to the 2025 seasonal spike.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 order intake or early-month registrations fell sharply below 2025 levels.

kept.name: September share of annual 2026 registrations
kept.rationale: September typically accounts for ~8-9% of annual German Pkw registrations; September 2025 (235,528) over full-year 2025 (~2.86M) is ~8.2%, consistent with this band.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of an unusual September 2026 seasonal distortion (e.g., a registration-date incentive cliff).

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
